title: Choosing a publicist
header_line: Jose's analysis of a book we are still naming. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: How would you know a publicist is worth the fee?
A student said that there are tiers: a freelancer or a team of two or three, a middle tier and an upper tier. It is good to know their connections and what they can deliver.
She said that the return is not as explicit as an ad with clicks, so you need other metrics to hold them accountable.
Jose said that if a publicist is abstract and noncommittal about results, you are in danger of losing your money. You want them specific about your audience and how they will get results.
A student said that the publications matter, what the results are after one article, and what they have done before. Other people's results are important, so ask for testimonials.
Jose said that a good publicist takes a big interest in your background, goals and messaging, and if they are not interested in learning who you are, that is a warning sign.

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what a publicist would have to deliver.
Write how you would measure it.
Write the questions you would ask for references.
Write the sign that would make you walk away.

check.q: What did Jose say about a publicist who is abstract on results?
choices: You are in danger of losing your money

check.q: What did a student say to ask for?
What did Jose say is a good sign?
choices: Interest in your background and goals

recap: Hold a publicist to specific results. Ask for proof.
